chunks: Ibn al-Walid, from Muhammad al-Attar, from al-Ash'ari, from al-Maythami, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abi Ayyub, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Jews asked the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) saying: Relate for us the genealogy of your Lord. So he remained three days not answering them, then this chapter was revealed to its end. I said: What is 'As-Samad'? He said: The one who is not hollow.

The Jews asked the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) saying: Relate for us the genealogy of your Lord. So he remained three days not answering them, then this chapter was revealed to its end. I said: What is 'As-Samad'? He said: The one who is not hollow.
ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'As-Samad' in Surah Al-Ikhlas according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) elucidates the term 'As-Samad' as 'the One who is not hollow' (ghayr majhuf), emphasizing God's absolute solidity and lack of physical cavity to refute anthropomorphic conceptions. It highlights the historical context of the Jews' challenge regarding the genealogy of God, which prompted the revelation of Surah Al-Ikhlas to establish divine transcendence beyond physical attributes.
